sources.entry: Claude Code Local by Matt Macosko - Runs Claude Code fully on-device on Apple Silicon: a native MLX server speaks the Anthropic Messages API, so the unmodified claude CLI works against local Qwen, Gemma and Llama models with no cloud calls. Includes RAM-based model selection, a tool-call parser for local models' output formats, and a verified-offline mode.

summary.one_liner: A local MLX server for Apple Silicon Macs that lets the unmodified Claude Code CLI run against open models (Qwen, Gemma, Llama, Hermes) on-device, with no cloud calls or API key, and a portable llama.cpp path for Linux and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: The core is proxy/server.py, a Python MLX server that speaks Anthropic's Messages API with streaming, so Claude Code talks to it directly without a translation layer. It converts each model's tool-call output format (Gemma 4, Qwen, Llama JSON) into Claude Code tool calls, attempts to repair malformed tool JSON, and reuses the prompt cache between turns. Setup scripts check the Mac's memory and pick a model that fits, download it, install the server, and create a Desktop launcher. The README also describes a "keep going" feature that resumes an existing Claude Code conversation on a free OpenRouter cloud model or a local model when Claude usage runs out. A Native Engine terminal agent (agent/agent.py) and a portable llama.cpp installer for Linux and Windows are also described. Tests for the tool-call parser are included.
use_cases: Run Claude Code offline on an Apple Silicon Mac
Keep coding when Claude usage limits are reached
Use local open-weight models as a Claude Code backend
Resume a Claude Code conversation on a different model
Run local coding models on Linux or Windows with llama.cpp
Keep code private by avoiding cloud model calls
how_to_run: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<local server URL> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-local claude --model claude-sonnet-4-6
notable: Speaks the Anthropic Messages API directly, with no OpenAI-to-Anthropic translation layer in between
Parses each local model's own tool-call format into Claude Code tool calls and repairs garbled tool JSON
Picks a model by available unified memory, from Gemma 4 E4B on 8 GB up to Qwen 3.8 27B at 96 GB and up
Resumes an existing Claude Code conversation on a free cloud or local model when usage limits are hit
Portable llama.cpp path for Linux and Windows with pinned builds and SHA-256 checks
caveats: The main engine requires Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and Python 3.12; Linux and Windows use a separate llama.cpp path
Free cloud models in keep-going send the conversation to OpenRouter and can be busy at times
The 8 GB tier model claimed to run a file it never wrote in the author's test, so tool use is unreliable there
Some modes need extra pieces that setup.sh does not install (browser agent, a speak command for voice)
keywords: local model backend for claude code
keep coding when claude limit reached
